Gaggle builds technology that helps K-12 schools identify student safety and wellness concerns so districts can intervene early, the kind of work our team is proud to say saves lives. We're hiring a detail-oriented HR Operations Coordinator to handle day-to-day HR operations: leave administration, onboarding and offboarding, compliance documentation, and the everyday work that keeps our employees and contractors covered. This is a hands-on execution role for someone who likes structure and staying on top of the details.

Key Responsibilities

Leave & Accommodation Administration

  • Administer Gaggle's in-house leave program, including tracking usage, documentation, and approvals/denials.
  • Track and apply state-specific paid leave programs that intersect with company leave policy, escalating questions as needed.
  • Provide timely communication of all leave needs with HR and Finance.
  • Maintain documentation for the ADA interactive process.

Employee & Contractor Administration

  • Handle onboarding and offboarding logistics for both employees and contractors, including contractor-specific recordkeeping requirements.
  • Own compliant I-9 verification and documentation for all new hires.
  • Manage background check workflow administration.
  • Own recruiting, candidate inquiries, and job postings.
  • Maintain a running list of state registrations, powers of attorney, and system logins across the states where we have teams.
  • Respond to employment verification requests as they come up.
  • Support the annual handbook review and Gaggle Compliance Month.

Compliance

  • Support required state and federal employment filings, including ACA, EEO-1, and Form 5500, by gathering documentation and tracking deadlines.
  • Assist in maintaining the multi-state contractor classification framework and making teams aware of the implications.
  • Serve as the point of contact for garnishment orders and other court documents, and support unemployment claims in partnership with our claims vendor.

HR Systems & Administrative Support

  • Maintain HR documentation and recordkeeping across systems, including contractor agreements, renewals/expirations, and required documentation.
  • Troubleshoot day-to-day issues with Paychex and other HR-related vendors.
  • Maintain and build out internal HR documentation and resources.
  • Assist with the annual performance review process.
  • Be the point person for routine contractor administration and escalated HR-system issues.
  • Pull and build HR reports, including custom reports, from Paychex as needed.
  • Track and document employee status changes (such as role, location, or classification changes) for recordkeeping purposes.
  • Provide general administrative support to HR and Finance, including vendor coordination, event logistics, holiday gifts, and responding to employer reviews.
  • Cross-train on core processes as needed to maintain continuity across the team.

Employee Relations

  • Serve as an empathetic, approachable first point of contact for employees with day-to-day HR questions or concerns.
  • Accurately and confidentially document any employee concerns that come your way, escalating anything sensitive or beyond routine.

Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of professional work experience, including 2+ years in HR with multi-state exposure.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Working knowledge of federal and multi-state employment fundamentals.
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills, excellent attention to detail.
  • Comfortable navigating Paychex (or a similarly complex HRIS platform) for day-to-day administration, including pulling standard and custom reports.
  • Hands-on experience with I-9 verification, unemployment claims, or wage garnishment processes.

Preferred

  • PHR (HRCI) or SHRM-CP certification, or actively working toward one.
  • Experience supporting contractor workforce administration.
  • Solid understanding of employee benefits (health, dental, vision, 401(k)).
  • Notary Public commission, or willingness to obtain one.

Core Competencies

  • You work independently and take full ownership of your tasks without needing close supervision.
  • You're detail-oriented, taking a "measure twice, hammer once" approach to ensure accuracy.
  • You look for what needs to get done or could be improved rather than waiting to be told.
  • You work through tasks quickly and consistently, rather than letting things pile up.
  • You're a self-directed learner who enjoys figuring out new systems and processes.
  • You want what is best for people, and it shows every time someone comes to you.

Salary Range and Benefits

Please apply to this posting in order to learn more about the starting salary range and benefit options. Some benefits highlights:

  • We’re a remote-first company; our team works together across all 50 US states
  • PPO and HDHP health insurance plans through BCBS of Illinois; coverage includes treatment for fertility (including IVF) as well as offering virtual visits and mental health resources
  • Dental insurance (including orthodontia) through Guardian
  • Vision insurance through BCBS/EyeMed
  • HSA, FSA, LPFSA, and DCFSA available, with a $500 annual company contribution
  • 401(k) plan with immediate vesting and a 4% company contribution with each paycheck
  • Employee Assistance Program through Paychex and Guardian (includes financial and legal assistance)
  • Flexible PTO
  • Generous, 100% to 70% paid leave plans, up to 90 days
  • Pet Insurance Discount Program
  • Fun perks such as team recognition programs, holiday gifts and bonuses, raffles, and fantasy football leagues

Our Team Commitment

Gaggle is proud to be recognized as a 2023 Top Workplace and also a proud recipient of the 2024 Top Workplaces USA Today award. We are committed to equal opportunity without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, or sex.

Social Media Marketing Manager

Remote | Brazil

Compensation: $9.00 to $15.00 USD/hour, based on experience

Schedule: 6 hours/day, Monday through Friday, with at least a 4-hour overlap during US business hours

Employment Type: Long-term, part-time contractor role with room to grow based on performance

About DrHouse

DrHouse is a fast-growing telehealth company making healthcare more accessible for patients across the United States.

Social media is a key part of our growth strategy. Our goal is not simply to gain followers. We create content that builds trust, educates consumers, and motivates people to use DrHouse when they need care.

The Role

We are looking for someone who thinks like a marketer, not just a social media coordinator.

This role requires previous experience managing social media for a healthcare, telehealth, health-tech, SaaS, or technology brand. You should understand how to create content that builds trust, educates audiences, and drives measurable business results in fast-paced, regulated industries.

You will build and manage 30-day campaigns that support our marketing strategy, seasonal healthcare trends, email campaigns, website content, product launches, promotions, and business priorities.

You should be comfortable taking ownership, identifying opportunities, and bringing new ideas to the table without waiting for detailed instructions.

If you need to be told exactly what to do every day, this is not the right role.

What You Will Own

  • Build and maintain a rolling 30-day content calendar that is always at least 30 days ahead.
  • Create engaging content for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Write platform-specific copy that sounds human, builds trust, and encourages people to take action.
  • Design graphics, carousels, reels, and short-form videos using Canva and other editing tools.
  • Align social content with ongoing email campaigns, website content, seasonal health needs, promotions, healthcare awareness moments, and timely reasons consumers may need telemedicine.
  • Create content that encourages US consumers to visit the website, download the app, start a consultation, and complete a telemedicine visit.
  • Repurpose content strategically across platforms instead of simply copying and pasting the same post everywhere.
  • Complete a minimum of 20 meaningful engagement activities every business day across LinkedIn and Instagram. Comments must be thoughtful, personalized, and add value. Generic or automated comments are not acceptable.
  • Maintain an engagement tracker with links to posts, engagement completed, target accounts, and recommended follow-up opportunities.
  • Monitor comments and messages on DrHouse content and draft timely responses.
  • Bring new campaign ideas, content opportunities, and organic growth experiments to the team.
  • Deliver a concise weekly report highlighting results, insights, recommendations, blockers, and priorities for the following week.
  • Communicate early when a deadline is at risk. Silence, missed follow-ups, and incomplete assignments are not acceptable.

Content Priorities

  • Three LinkedIn posts per week.
  • Three Instagram posts per week, with selected content repurposed for Facebook.
  • Two short-form videos per week, repurposed for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Daily LinkedIn and Instagram engagement.
  • Timely responses to comments on published posts.

Success Measures

  • Qualified organic traffic from social media.
  • Website visits, app downloads, consultations started, and completed telemedicine visits influenced by social campaigns.
  • Engagement quality and relevant audience growth.
  • Consistently meeting deadlines and maintaining a 30-day-ahead content calendar.
  • Proactive ideas that improve content performance and business results.

Approval & Quality Standards

Initially, all calendars, copy, graphics, and videos must be submitted for approval before publishing. Greater publishing autonomy may be provided after you demonstrate strong judgment, consistency, and knowledge of the DrHouse brand.

You are responsible for checking spelling, links, formatting, brand consistency, and accuracy before submitting work.

Because we operate in healthcare, all content must be accurate, responsible, and aligned with approved company messaging. Unsupported health claims will not be published.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 3+ years of experience managing social media for a healthcare, telehealth, health-tech, SaaS, or technology brand.
  • Proven experience creating social media campaigns that produced measurable business results.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating successful campaigns, content creation, and audience growth.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Strong copywriting skills with the ability to create engaging, platform-specific content.
  • Advanced Canva skills and experience creating graphics, carousels, reels, and short-form videos.
  • Experience editing short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Strong understanding of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube best practices.
  • Experience using analytics to optimize content performance and make data-driven decisions.
  • A sharp visual eye and strong attention to detail.
  • Highly organized, self-directed, proactive, and able to work independently without constant supervision.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with US healthcare or telehealth companies.
  • Experience marketing healthcare, SaaS, or technology products to US consumers.
  • Experience supporting demand generation, product launches, or performance marketing campaigns.

AI can support research and ideation, but generic or unedited AI-generated content is not a fit.

To Apply

Please include the following with your application:

  • Your resume highlighting your experience managing social media for a healthcare, telehealth, health-tech, SaaS, or technology company.
  • Three to five examples of social campaigns or content you personally created.
  • Briefly explain your role in creating each example.
  • Share the measurable results each campaign or piece of content produced.
  • Include links to social media accounts or content you currently manage.
  • List the tools you use for graphics, video editing, scheduling, engagement, and analytics.
  • Share your availability during US business hours.
  • Provide your requested hourly rate.

Final candidates will be invited to complete a short paid assessment involving social media strategy, copywriting, and creative execution.

Salary: $9 – $15 / hour

Our client, an international e-commerce company with a strong presence in the USA, is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Inventory & Logistics Specialist to oversee end-to-end supply chain and inventory operations. This full-time remote role combines freight management, Amazon FBA coordination, inventory forecasting, and reverse logistics to ensure smooth operations across all sales channels. If you are experienced in e-commerce logistics, Amazon fulfillment, and supply chain optimization, and enjoy working in a fast-paced, high-impact environment, wed love to hear from you.

About the company:

The company is a premium pet brand known for its high-quality, durable bulky pet products and accessories. Built for both professionals and devoted pet owners, the brands products are designed with attention to detail, functionality, and longevity. The brand is committed to creating elevated, practical experiences for pets and their people—and is looking for an Inventory & Logistics Specialist to help scale that mission by ensuring seamless product flow from factory to customer.

Key Responsibilities:

Freight & Supply Chain Management

  • Manage end-to-end order placement with factories and track order progress through to completion.
  • Request, negotiate, and select the best quotes from freight forwarders, determining the optimal type of sea freight for each specific situation.
  • Design ideal loading configurations for shipping containers based on product dimensions to maximize space and reduce shipping costs.
  • Oversee the loading process through active communication with factories and freight partners.
  • Track all global shipments, proactively flagging and mitigating any potential delays.

Amazon FBA & E-commerce Operations

  • Create and manage Amazon Shipments, utilizing software solutions (e.g., 9Yards and similar simulation tools) to run multiple simulations and target the most cost-effective Amazon warehouses.
  • Oversee the receiving of units at both Amazon fulfillment centers and partner 3PL warehouses.
  • Perform thorough reconciliation for all inbound shipments to ensure accurate stock levels and file claims for missing units when necessary.
  • Coordinate Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) orders for Last Mile transport from our 3PL to customers for non-Amazon (DTC/B2B) orders.

Inventory Forecasting & Management

  • Continuously monitor inventory levels across all sales channels to prevent overstocking or Out-of-Stock (OOS) situations.
  • Forecast inventory movements and project OOS dates at the SKU level to accurately plan factory order quantities.

Reverse Logistics & Returns Management

  • Create and manage Amazon removal orders for customer returns.
  • Arrange transport from Amazon to 3PL/processing facilities.
  • Oversee the de-kitting, inspection, and sorting of damaged units into tiers for parts harvesting or resale.

Scale of Operations:

  • Container Shipments: ~8 per month.
  • LTL Orders (Last Mile): ~10 per week.
  • Factory Orders: ~6 per year.

Software & Workflow Proficiency:

  • Amazon FBA & E-commerce Systems: Deep expertise with Amazon Seller Central, FBA placement optimization, inbound reconciliation, and removal/disposal orders.
  • Forecasting & Inventory Management: Hands-on experience with IMS tools (SoStocked, RestockPro, Cin7, Skubana), advanced Excel or Google Sheets for SKU-level forecasting and run-rate models.
  • Logistics, Freight & 3PL Integration: Familiarity with container load planning software (EasyCargo, CubeMaster), freight platforms (Flexport, Freightos), warehouse management systems (ShipStation, ShipHero), and reverse logistics workflows.

Core Competencies

  • 3+ years of experience in supply chain, logistics, or Amazon inventory management.
  • Proven ability to manage complex shipments and multi-stage fulfillment workflows across international markets.
  • Strong understanding of Amazon FBA processes and multi-channel e-commerce operations.
  • Advanced analytical mindset with the ability to build and interpret detailed SKU-level forecasting and inventory models.
  • Practical experience coordinating international freight, container shipments, and 3PL operations in a multi-channel environment.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and high attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently while coordinating with multiple stakeholders.
  • Alignment with the companys premium brand standards and operational excellence mindset.

Why Join Us:

  • Play a critical role in ensuring smooth operations for a high-ticket pet brand on Amazon.
  • Own inventory planning, logistics, and fulfillment workflows.
  • Work remotely from anywhere.
  • Competitive salary and flexible working hours.
  • Collaborate with a creative, forward-thinking team dedicated to innovation in the pet space.
  • Make a tangible impact on a brand that values quality, customer experience, and operational excellence.

jobs.excerpt: About FloatFloat is the full-stack platform for Specialty Pharma home infusion.
jobs.description:
About Float

Float is the full-stack platform for Specialty Pharma home infusion. We’re on a mission to make healthcare safer, easier, and more efficient by connecting SuperNurses to home medication visits - moving all care that doesn’t need a hospital to the home.

Float connects nurses with patients so they can get treatments for their chronic conditions in the home rather than going into the overcrowded hospital. Our model benefits all stakeholders - patients get more convenient care, nurses access flexible work for better pay, pharmacies fill more prescriptions, hospitals reduce low-reimbursement admissions, and payors enjoy 12x reduced costs with home-delivered care.

Over the last 5 years, we’ve successfully demonstrated multi-state expansion, validated strong unit economics, and boast remarkable retention of patients, nurses, and pharmacies. We’ve facilitated over 100,000 patient visits with 1,100 nurses and are scaling our platform, team, and operations to serve more geographies and patients.

Float Health is currently recruiting nurses and serving patients in California, Nevada, Arizona, Texas, Washington, Michigan, Indiana, Georgia, and Ohio with several new states on the horizon.

The Role

As an Intake Specialist, you’ll play a key role in our operations and customer success by managing new patient referrals and coordinating timely start-of-care visits. These visits are typically more urgent than routine healthcare appointments, so your ability to act quickly, communicate clearly, and manage details with precision will directly impact patient outcomes and satisfaction.

You’ll serve as a liaison between specialty pharmacies, nurses, and patients—leveraging technology platforms to ensure smooth coordination, timely staffing, and successful care delivery. This is an externally facing role that requires excellent organizational skills, strong attention to detail, and a proactive, solution-oriented mindset.

Customer service is central to this position. As the first point of contact for patients, pharmacies, and nurses, you’ll represent Float Health with empathy, professionalism, and efficiency. Your ability to resolve issues quickly and accurately will help build trust and drive a seamless experience for all stakeholders.

You’ll contribute to achieving company goals by making staffing decisions aligned with operational and financial objectives. You’ll need to be flexible and adaptable as priorities shift. We're looking for someone who is highly engaged and eager to identify opportunities to improve our workflows, technology, and overall user experience.

Who you are

  • You’re flexible and have a learner mindset: we’re a start up, we move fast and are constantly improving.
  • You thrive in urgency: our patients are sometimes discharged directly from the hospital to home visits on short notice, you are a key part of their care delivery.
  • You’re team-oriented: in a remote role, strong teammate connections are more important than ever.
  • You have a strong sense of accountability and integrity: external customers and internal team members will rely on you everyday.

What you’ll do:

  • Utilize the Float Health platform and supporting technology (Zendesk, Google Suite, Slack) to coordinate start of care visits, including:
    • Collecting information from pharmacies and patients
    • Matching appropriate nurses to patients
    • Managing offers in our marketplace to ensure we pay the nurses a responsible rate
    • Onboarding patients to Float Health
    • Confirming logistics and schedules with all users to ensure a safe and seamless home visit
    • Responding to restaff and reschedule requests as they arise
  • Communicate clearly, kindly, and proactively with specialty pharmacies, nurses, and patients via email, phone calls, chat, and SMS
    • Respond to Inbound phone calls, emails, chat, and SMS as well as initiating outbound
  • Work cross functionally with internal teams in shared queues and Slack to ensure visit documentation and other visit related tasks are completed
  • Prioritize and coordinate multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Learn new processes and technology continuously
  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with peers at specialty pharmacies
  • Complete tasks related to pharmacy engagement as needed
  • Provide feedback to improve our technology and processes

Required skills:

  • 1+ years of experience with medical scheduling
  • Ability to utilize multiple technology platforms simultaneously
  • Ability to manage inbound communication while supporting other tasks
  • Ability to type 60 words per minute with high accuracy
  • Excellent critical thinking and problem-solving abilities
  • Highly organized with excellent time management skills
  • Exceptional customer service skills
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to digest and explain complex information clearly to all users
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment

Preferred experience:

  • Proficiency in medical terminology and policies and prior experience in the healthcare industry is highly desirable
  • Previous infusion therapy, healthcare intake, or specialty pharmacy experience preferred
  • Previous start up experience is preferred

Location and Schedule

Location: This is a fully remote position based in the US.

Employment Type: This is a full time position working 40 hours per week. We are looking for someone who can work weekends as part of their regular schedule for this role.

Work Hours: Float operates in the PST time zone. This role is expected to work Sunday–Thursday, with shifts typically running 9am–5pm or 11am–7pm PST.

Benefits:

  • Medical, dental, vision
  • 401k matching
  • Unlimited PTO with minimum days
  • Paid parental leave
  • Home office setup
  • Phone & internet monthly stipend
  • Annual Learning Stipend
  • HSA & FSA
  • Voluntary Life, Accident, Hospital, and Critical Illness Insurance
  • 100% remote (within the US)

Compensation:

Compensation for this role consists of a base salary and options grant, with the base salary expected to range from $48,000 to $50,000. Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience and skills.

Culture:

We’re a Series A startup looking for individuals who are willing to grow with the team and adapt to our fast-paced, ever changing work environment.

At Float, we #WorkfortheSuperNurse. We believe that making the best nurses the heroes attracts the best talent, and in turn delivers the best patient experience. As our nurses boldly do what’s right for our patients, we boldly do what’s right for them. If this is a purpose that inspires you, we’d love to talk!

Float Health is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate the diversity of the team that builds for diverse users. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Salary: $48,000 – $50,000 / year

jobs.description:
Reports to: Engineering Manager

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $200,000 - $220,000 base plus bonus and equity

What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 5M endpoints and 14M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

About the Team

Huntress protects the small and mid-sized businesses that attackers assume can't afford a security team. The Detection Platform team builds the engines and pipelines that turn billions of raw telemetry events into the signals our 24/7 SOC acts on. Every detection Huntress ships, across endpoint, identity, SIEM, and third-party EDR, runs through systems this team owns. We measure ourselves on two things: time to detection and detection engine uptime.

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to help build and rebuild these systems without disrupting the SOC that depends on them, and to make their behavior predictable under load. This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you'll lead major workstreams, set direction that other engineering teams build against, and write and review production code every week.

What You'll Own

  • Detection engine and pipeline modernization. We're rewriting our detection engine to support the full Sigma v2 specification, including stateful correlation of patterns across many events over time. In parallel, we're reworking several existing detection pipelines and building new ones, moving off the bespoke per-product detectors we've accumulated and onto a common platform. You'll lead major workstreams across both and own the validation approach that proves a reworked pipeline still behaves like the one it replaces, so we can turn old paths off knowing we haven't lost anything.
  • Reliability and behavior under load. A detection pipeline that quietly stops producing signals is worse than one that crashes loudly, and detection volume spikes for reasons we don't always control. You'll build the guarantees that make quiet failure impossible: end-to-end latency measurement, liveness coverage, and alerting that fires when expected work stops arriving. You'll also build the mechanisms that keep a spike bounded and recoverable.
  • Event schemas and data contracts. Our schema and transformer layer are what several other engineering teams build their detections against. You'll help drive toward a coherent internal standard and build the validation and drift-detection tooling that catches upstream changes before they break detections.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Deep experience designing, building, and operating production distributed systems at scale, primarily in Go, with the range to work across several layers of the stack.
  • You have replaced or substantially re-architected a live, high-throughput system without breaking its consumers, and you can walk us through how you proved the new path was equivalent, staged the cut-over, and decided it was safe to retire the old one.
  • Experience with high-volume event or data pipelines, and a good feel for how they behave under load: where things queue, where they fall behind, and what happens to correctness when they do.
  • Strong operability instincts. You design observability in rather than retrofitting it, and you've built alerting that catches the absence of expected work, not just errors.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership across team boundaries. You've set a direction that other teams had to build against and raised the engineering bar around you, without needing positional authority.
  • Judgment about production quality: when a system is good enough to ship, when it needs more evaluation, and when it shouldn't ship at all.
  • Hands-on experience with AI coding tools, and a point of view on using them well, where correctness is a security outcome.

Strongly Preferred

  • A background in security operations or security engineering: time spent writing or tuning detections, or working in a SOC. You know what makes a detection maintainable, how fast noise erodes a SOC's trust in its tooling, and why a missed detection is a different class of failure than a noisy one.
  • Experience with detection-as-code or other rule- and DSL-driven systems, including the parsing and evaluation work that supporting a specification properly entails.
  • Experience building platform tooling for non-engineer authors such as rule writers, analysts, and researchers, where the product surface is a language, an API, and a feedback loop.
  • Ruby on Rails experience. Some of our pipeline and application code is Rails, and you'll occasionally read and review Ruby. It's a nice-to-have, not a requirement; we'll help you ramp.

Our Stack

You'll work primarily in Go across our detection engines, pipelines, and the services around them, with Kafka, Temporal, Redis, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and Kubernetes across AWS and Azure. Some of our pipeline and application code is Ruby on Rails. Detection logic is written in Sigma.

We don't expect prior experience with all of it, and we're not screening on the list; Go is the one language we'll assess directly in interviews. You should be someone who likes being fluent across a broad stack rather than being specialized in one corner of it.

What We Offer:

  • 100% remote work environment - since our founding in 2015
  • Generous paid time off policy, including vacation, sick time, and paid holidays
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Highly competitive and comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits plans
  • 401(k) with a 5% contribution regardless of employee contribution
  • Life and Disability insurance plans
  • Stock options for all full-time employees
  • One-time $500 reimbursement for building/upgrading home office
  • Annual allowance for education and professional development assistance
  • $75 USD/month digital reimbursement
  • Access to the BetterUp platform for coaching, personal, and professional growth

Huntress is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where every single member of our team is valued, has a voice, and is empowered to come to work every day just as they are.

We do not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

We do discriminate against hackers who try to exploit businesses of all sizes.

We're hiring a Performance Marketing Graphic Designer to own static ad creative across Meta, Google Display, and Native platforms. You'll design thumb-stopping statics, build out high-volume variations to test hooks and angles, and treat every ad as a conversion problem to solve — not just a layout to make pretty. The goal is simple: statics that win at the auction and scale.

If you understand why one headline-and-image combination crushes while a more "designed" version flops — and you've got the data instinct to know the difference — this role is for you. And if you can code, you'll have room to build things most designers can't.

What You'll Do

  • Design high-converting static ads for Meta (Facebook/Instagram), Google Display, and Native platforms — optimized for thumb-stop rate, CTR, and ROAS, not just visual polish.
  • Produce creative variations at volume — multiple hooks, headlines, layouts, and angles per concept so the media team always has fresh statics in rotation for testing.
  • Master the direct-response static formats that actually perform: native/editorial-style ads, advertorials, before/after, comparison charts, social proof and review layouts, infographic ads, and UGC-style statics.
  • Win the feed in the first glance with strong visual hierarchy, punchy headlines, and design that communicates the value prop instantly.
  • Use AI image tools (Midjourney, Firefly, DALL·E, Ideogram, or similar) to expand concepting speed and generate assets, backgrounds, and variations.
  • Work the data. Review creative performance (CTR, CVR, ROAS, thumb-stop rate) and iterate your designs based on what's actually converting.
  • Collaborate closely with media buyers, strategists, and copywriters on audience insights, product positioning, and funnel strategy.
  • Stay current on platform specs, ad formats, design trends, and ad-policy/compliance requirements across channels (including health-adjacent advertising standards where relevant).

Coding / HTML — A Big Plus

This isn't required, but it's a real differentiator and you'll get to use it:

  • Build HTML/CSS ad components, end cards, and interactive units.
  • Design and code advertorials, sales pages, and landing pages that match the ad creative and convert.
  • Create templated, dynamic systems so static variations can be produced at scale instead of one-by-one.
  • HTML email design and build.

If you live in Figma and are comfortable in code, tell us — it moves you to the top of the stack.

What Success Looks Like

  • First 30 days: You're shipping clean, on-brief static ads with fast turnaround and learning our brands, accounts, and creative testing process.
  • First 90 days: You're independently producing testable static variations across formats and proposing hooks and angles based on what the data is telling us.
  • Ongoing: Your statics consistently produce winners that scale — and you can point to the metrics that prove it.

What You Bring

  • 2–4 years designing static creative for paid social and performance marketing (agency or in-house DTC/ecommerce experience strongly preferred).
  • Expert command of Figma and the Adobe suite (Photoshop, Illustrator), plus hands-on experience with AI image generation tools.
  • A real understanding of direct-response advertising — hooks, angles, offer structure, visual hierarchy, and the psychology of what makes someone stop scrolling and click.
  • Channel fluency: you've designed specifically for Meta Ads Manager, Google Display, and Native networks, and you understand the spec and behavior differences between them.
  • Speed without sloppiness — you thrive on quick turnarounds, high output, and iterative testing cycles.
  • A portfolio of high-performing static ad creative, ideally with the campaign results or metrics to back it up.

Bonus Points

  • HTML/CSS and front-end coding ability (see above — this is the big one).
  • Familiarity with advertorial, sales page, and landing page design.
  • Light motion or animated static (GIF/HTML) experience.
  • Knowledge of A/B testing frameworks and creative optimization cycles.
  • A track record collaborating directly with media buyers, performance marketers, and copywriters.

jobs.excerpt: Vividly is the leading modern trade promotion management (TPM) solution built by and for the consumer packaged goods industry.
jobs.description:
Vividly is the leading modern trade promotion management (TPM) solution built by and for the consumer packaged goods industry. From campaign creation to deductions management and promotion measurement, we help brands manage every element of trade spend. With our easy-to-use platform and industry-leading experience, we pride ourselves on our ability to bring businesses to the next level.

Not familiar with trade promotion spend? That’s OK. Most people aren’t. It’s an $8 trillion dollar problem that is ripe for disruption by an innovative SaaS startup. In order to grow, consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands spend 20% of their topline revenue to get into retailers and promote their products within those retailers. The problem is that today 70% of those promotions are not ROI positive. This is because ROI is hard to track. The industry operates on emails, pdfs, and xls spreadsheets. At Vividly, we’re solving this massive problem with exciting tactics including AI, Machine Learning, and Fintech and adding value to everyone in the chain. Some of our customers include brands you may use and love - Liquid Death, Amy’s, and Perfect Snacks.

We’re looking for a Solutions Architect who can bridge the gap between what our customers need to accomplish and how Vividly should be designed to support them.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys understanding complex business processes, challenging the status quo, and turning customer requirements into scalable future-state solutions. You’ll work across business processes, accounting workflows, data, integrations, and Vividly configuration to ensure our customers are set up correctly from the beginning.

The Solutions Architect is a critical part of our customer onboarding experience. You’ll help preserve continuity from Sales through Implementation, ensure requirements are understood before teams begin building, and keep multiple implementation work streams aligned around one cohesive solution.

What You'll Achieve

As a Solutions Architect, you’ll become an expert in Vividly, CPG trade workflows, customer business processes, ERP ecosystems, and how our different solutions come together.

You’ll engage early in the customer journey to understand what was sold, why the customer purchased Vividly, and what outcomes they expect to achieve. Following Closed Won, you’ll lead Solution Alignment to validate requirements, future-state workflows, technical dependencies, assumptions, and implementation scope before execution begins.

You’ll design solutions across areas such as Trade Promotion Management, Deduction Management, Cash Application, accruals, forecasting, revenue data, master data, file retrieval, and ERP integrations. You won't personally configure every workflow or build every integration. Instead, you'll create the solution blueprint that enables Implementation, Integrations, Managed Services, and Customer Success to execute successfully.

Throughout onboarding, you’ll remain the owner of solution integrity, helping resolve ambiguity, evaluate changes, and ensure individual work streams don't make decisions that compromise the overall customer solution.

Beyond individual implementations, you’ll identify recurring patterns, process gaps, and opportunities to standardize how Vividly designs and delivers solutions so that onboarding becomes increasingly faster, more predictable, and scalable.

In This Role, You'll Help The Team:

  • Review pre-sales discovery, commitments, requirements, and proposed solutions to ensure continuity from Sales into onboarding.
  • Lead customer Solution Alignment sessions to validate business objectives, requirements, workflows, dependencies, assumptions, and success criteria.
  • Understand customers' current-state processes and design scalable future-state workflows using Vividly.
  • Translate customer requirements into clear solution designs that Implementation, Integrations, Managed Services, and Customer Success can execute against.
  • Design solutions across trade planning, deductions, Cash Application, accruals, forecasting, reporting, pricing, customer/product hierarchies, revenue, and related workflows.
  • Understand how Vividly fits within the customer's broader ecosystem, including ERP systems, banks, retailer/distributor data, syndicated data, and other business systems.
  • Partner with Integration Solutions Engineering to define integration requirements, data flows, system dependencies, cadence, and technical constraints.
  • Partner with Managed Services to define document retrieval, deduction, and operational requirements.
  • Define clear requirements and acceptance criteria before configuration or development begins.
  • Identify potential implementation risks, dependencies, scope gaps, and product limitations early enough to prevent downstream rework.
  • Maintain clear documentation of solution decisions, workflows, requirements, assumptions, and dependencies.
  • Provide Implementation with an actionable blueprint for portal configuration and customer setup.
  • Remain engaged throughout onboarding to answer design questions and resolve ambiguity without taking over day-to-day project management.
  • Evaluate new requirements discovered during implementation and determine whether they represent configuration changes, integration requirements, product gaps, or changes in scope.
  • Support change-order and re-scoping conversations when customer requirements materially differ from the approved solution.
  • Participate in critical implementation checkpoints, design reviews, UAT, and go-live readiness when solution validation is required.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring customer requirements, product gaps, and opportunities to improve Vividly's capabilities.
  • Help establish reusable solution patterns, implementation standards, discovery frameworks, and best practices that reduce customization and accelerate onboarding.
  • Ensure critical solution context transfers cleanly to Customer Success so customers don't lose continuity after go-live.

You May Be A Good Fit For The Role If You:

  • Have 4+ years of experience in Solution Architecture, Solutions Consulting, Implementation Consulting, Business Systems, ERP consulting, CPG technology, or a similar customer-facing role.
  • Have experience understanding complex business processes and translating them into scalable system or workflow designs.
  • Can move comfortably between business requirements and technical conversations without needing to personally engineer every solution.
  • Understand financial or operational workflows such as deductions, accounts receivable, accruals, revenue, forecasting, reconciliation, or accounting.
  • Have experience with ERP systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Sage, QuickBooks, or similar platforms.
  • Understand integration concepts including APIs, data flows, field mappings, master data, authentication, and system dependencies.
  • Can facilitate complex conversations involving Accounting, Finance, Sales, Operations, IT, and executive stakeholders.
  • Are comfortable challenging existing processes and recommending a better future-state approach rather than simply recreating what a customer does today.
  • Can distinguish between a business requirement, configuration requirement, integration requirement, product gap, and scope change.
  • Have strong documentation skills and can turn ambiguous conversations into clear requirements and decisions.
  • Are comfortable working directly with customers and establishing credibility as a trusted advisor.
  • Can manage ambiguity, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and know when additional expertise is required.
  • Learn quickly and can develop expertise across new products, workflows, ERP systems, and customer use cases.
  • Are highly organized and capable of maintaining context across multiple complex customer implementations.
  • Are comfortable operating in a fast-paced startup environment where processes are evolving and you'll help improve them.
  • Have strong judgment, executive presence, and communication skills.
  • Want to have a foundational impact on how a growing SaaS organization delivers complex customer solutions.

Experience with CPG, Trade Promotion Management, Deduction Management, Cash Application, Sales Finance, or CPG accounting is strongly preferred, but we would also consider candidates with strong solution architecture experience in adjacent financial or operational SaaS environments who demonstrate the ability to learn the industry quickly.

How You'll Work

You’ll work closely with Solutions Engineering, Implementation, Integrations, Managed Services, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering.

Our operating model is built around a simple principle: Solutions Engineering determines how Vividly can solve the customer's problem. Solution Architecture defines how that solution should operate. Our delivery teams make it happen.

You'll typically enter the customer journey during late-stage solutioning or immediately following Closed Won. Your first responsibility is to establish Solution Alignment, ensuring the customer's objectives, workflows, scope, requirements, and technical dependencies are understood before teams begin execution.

From there:

Implementation owns the project plan, customer coordination, configuration, milestones, and overall execution.

Integration Solutions Engineering determines how systems connect and owns the technical integration workstream.

Managed Services establishes and operates applicable retrieval and managed workflows.

Customer Success owns adoption, value realization, and the long-term customer relationship.

You own the integrity of the solution across those workstreams.

There will naturally be overlap. We expect Solutions Architects to understand enough about configuration, integrations, accounting, and customer operations to make informed recommendations and identify when something isn't working. At the same time, you won't be expected to personally manage every project task, configure every customer environment, or build every integration.

The goal is to give customers one cohesive solution rather than a collection of disconnected workstreams, while giving our delivery teams the clarity they need to execute quickly and confidently.

What Success Looks Like

You'll know you're succeeding when:

  • Customers don't have to restart discovery after Closed Won.
  • Solution Alignment identifies material requirements and risks before configuration or integration work begins.
  • Delivery teams understand exactly what they're building and why.
  • Fewer requirements are discovered late in implementation.
  • Rework and mid-implementation scope changes decrease.
  • Portal, Integration, and Managed Services workstreams remain aligned to one solution.
  • Customers are guided toward scalable Vividly best practices rather than unnecessarily recreating legacy processes.
  • Implementation timelines become shorter and more predictable.
  • Customer Success receives clear context on the solution, customer objectives, and operating model at handoff.
  • Customers reach value faster because Vividly was designed correctly from the beginning.

Why Choose Vividly?

A modern, remote-first workplace

We are committed to succeeding as a fully remote team, empowering you with the flexibility to thrive, no commute required. Every Vividly team member receives a stipend upon hire to help create a comfortable, productive home office.

Vividly days off & flexible PTO

For most USA holidays that fall on a Monday or Friday, we turn it into a 4 day weekend! Vividly also offers Flexible Time Off (and we really mean it) to help prevent burn out and fuel creativity.

Competitive Benefits

  • Healthcare, Dental and Vision - We cover 100% of your monthly premiums and 50% of all dependents
  • 401(k) - With a 3% employer contribution
  • Weekly $20 Sharebite Meal Stipend - For every meal you purchase, they donate a meal through Feeding America!
  • Monthly $50 Wellness Reimbursement
  • Monthly $200 Remote Work Stipend

Commitment to our values - The Vividly Code

  • Kind Ambition -We push boundaries with empathy and integrity
  • Keep It Real - We are transparent, honest, and authentic
  • Customer Love - We act as trusted advisors to our customers
  • Own It - We take responsibility and drive outcomes
  • Urgency Wins - We move quickly and focus on impact
  • Pull Together - We collaborate to win as a team

Please note: Vividly will never request sensitive information such as your social security number, bank account information, or other non-publicly available information during the application and interview process. If an applicant is extended an offer of employment, such sensitive information will be requested at that time during the onboarding process. Vividly will never ask you to receive and ship packages or goods as part of the interview. Other practices to be on alert for:

  • Contact initiated via unsolicited text message or cold call. Vividly does not follow up with candidates through instant messaging applications.
  • Our Talent Acquisition team only corresponds from email addresses with the domain ‘@govividly.com’. If a generic email ID ending with Gmail/Yahoo or other domain is used while receiving a job offer or interview call, there is a likelihood of a scammer.

jobs.excerpt: About the CompanyBased in San Diego, California, Eyes On Eyecare is a technology and healthcare information company shaping the future of eyecare.
jobs.description:
About the Company

Based in San Diego, California, Eyes On Eyecare is a technology and healthcare information company shaping the future of eyecare. Through brands like Eyes On Dry Eye, Glance, and npiQ, we deliver web applications, accredited education, and data products to tens of thousands of eyecare professionals. Our mission is to support the people who care for vision with the tools, knowledge, and connections they need to do their best work.

Visionary Medical Education (VME) is our accredited independent medical education partner, delivering continuing education programming for optometrists and ophthalmologists across the United States that is accredited by the Council on Optometric Practitioner Education (COPE) and works with partner organization’s to deliver ACCME accredited education.

About the Role

The Director, Clinical Education is the clinical and scientific backbone of VME's educational programming. You own the educational product end to end, from needs assessment and curriculum architecture through faculty selection, learning design, program execution, and outcomes measurement. You are the reason Medical Affairs teams trust that an accredited grant translates into rigorous, independent, high-quality education.

This role is built for a clinician or clinical educator with deep ophthalmic or optometric expertise who has moved into medical education and wants to build something substantial. You bring strong research and analytical instincts, working fluency across the full clinical landscape of eyecare, and the ability to translate complex science into rigorous, practical education that changes how clinicians think and practice.

You will work closely with the Director, Grant Revenue and Supporter Relations to develop educational concepts that address documented practice gaps. You serve as the scientific and educational lead throughout the program lifecycle, from gap analysis through curriculum delivery and outcomes reporting. Educational content, faculty selection, and learning objectives are determined independently of commercial supporters, and protecting that independence is part of the work.

Key Responsibilities

Educational Strategy and Curriculum Development

  • Lead the design and development of accredited continuing education programming for optometrists and ophthalmologists across the full clinical landscape of eyecare, including anterior segment, cornea and ocular surface, dry eye and meibomian gland disease, glaucoma, retina, refractive, neuro-ophthalmology, pediatrics, and emerging therapeutic areas.
  • Conduct rigorous needs assessments using peer-reviewed literature, survey data, claims data, publication trends, and clinician feedback to identify genuine clinical practice gaps.
  • Develop measurable learning objectives that meet educational design standards and align with ACCME and COPE accreditation requirements.
  • Select and justify educational formats based on identified gaps and audience needs, including live symposia, enduring online modules, hybrid programs, case-based learning, and other delivery models.
  • Translate clinical evidence and emerging science into clear, actionable educational experiences that move learners toward competence and performance change.

Program Design and Educational Materials

  • Lead the design and build of educational assets across program types, including slide decks, faculty briefing documents, case studies, panel and roundtable formats, enduring materials, and live program flow and structure.
  • Set and enforce visual, narrative, and scientific quality standards across all VME educational materials.
  • Partner with content and design teams to ensure that the look, structure, and learner experience of every program reflects the rigor of accredited education.
  • Oversee the development of speaker materials, pre-work, learner guides, post-program resources, and any other materials that support the educational objectives of a given program.

Research and Clinical Evidence

  • Maintain working fluency across the breadth of clinical eyecare and deep expertise in one or more therapeutic areas, with the ability to read, evaluate, and synthesize the primary literature.
  • Lead the scientific underpinning of every VME program by sourcing, vetting, and integrating the strongest available evidence into needs assessments, learning objectives, and content.
  • Track emerging clinical evidence, regulatory developments, and standard of care evolution across major therapeutic areas in eyecare.
  • Translate complex clinical research into rigorous educational design without losing scientific accuracy.

Faculty and Key Opinion Leader Relationships

  • Build and maintain a strong network of key opinion leaders (KOLs) and clinical faculty across optometry and ophthalmology.
  • Identify, vet, and manage faculty for accredited programs in compliance with ACCME and COPE independence standards.
  • Support faculty in developing scientifically rigorous, clinically relevant content that is free of commercial bias.
  • Represent VME at ophthalmic society meetings, including the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO), the American Optometric Association (AOA), the American Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery (ASCRS), the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO), and others.

Outcomes Measurement and Reporting

  • Design and implement outcomes measurement strategies up to Levels 4 and 5, including pre and post knowledge assessments, competence measures, and performance change tracking.
  • Collaborate on outcomes data analysis to produce evidence-based reports for supporters and accrediting bodies.
  • Continuously improve evaluation frameworks so that data collection is meaningful, rigorous, and aligned with accreditation requirements.
  • Contribute to the scientific quality and narrative integrity of all educational outcomes reports.

Compliance, Accreditation, and Educational Integrity

  • Serve as the internal expert on COPE accreditation standards for optometric continuing education and ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence for continuing medical education.
  • Maintain the firewall between educational content development and commercial supporter influence in every aspect of the work.
  • Oversee faculty disclosure management, conflict of interest review, and content independence processes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the Director, Grant Revenue and Supporter Relations to develop educational concepts grounded in clinical evidence and aligned with identified practice gaps.
  • Contribute clinical and scientific expertise to grant proposals, including needs assessments, learning objectives, and outcomes frameworks.
  • Collaborate with VME events and technology teams on program delivery and learner experience for accredited programming.
  • Provide clinical review and quality oversight for all accredited educational content.

Who This Role Is For

This role is the right fit if you:

  • Are a clinician or clinical educator who wants to build a credible, rigorous medical education function and is ready to make that the center of your professional life.
  • Read and synthesize primary clinical literature regularly and treat research strength as a core part of the job.
  • Hold deep expertise in one or more therapeutic areas of eyecare and have working fluency across the full clinical landscape.
  • Take real pride in the craft of educational design, including the structure of a program, the quality of a slide deck, and the experience of a learner.
  • Have a strong network of clinical thought leaders and enjoy building and maintaining those relationships.
  • Understand and respect the ACCME and COPE frameworks and view educational independence as a feature of the work.
  • Operate well in an entrepreneurial environment where playbooks, templates, and quality standards are still being built.

Who This Role Is Not For

At Terrestris, we leverage technology to create better mission outcomes through better human performance. We form strong client and team relationships through transparency and strive to create an environment where our team can let their excellence shine through. By finding, developing, and incorporating new ideas, we provide memorable services. Rooted in the USMC values of honor, courage, and commitment, Terrestris seeks to deliver extraordinary value to the American people by helping the Government become more efficient and effective.

So, what will the Adjunct Faculty Instructorat Terrestris do?

The Adjunct Faculty Instructor NAV 101 supports the U.S. Naval Community College (USNCC) by delivering high-quality, fully online asynchronous instruction to enlisted Sailors, Marines, and Coast Guardsmen pursuing college-level education. Faculty members teach Naval Studies and/or General Education courses that strengthen critical thinking, leadership, communication, and operational readiness while supporting the Navy's mission of developing a highly educated and mission-ready force.

USNCC courses are delivered through the Blackboard Learning Management System (LMS) in an 8-week online format. Faculty provide engaging instruction, evaluate student performance, facilitate discussions, and deliver timely, meaningful feedback while maintaining the highest standards of academic excellence and professionalism.

What does a typical day look like for an Adjunct Faculty Instructor?

You will:

  • Attend required onboarding and course orientation prior to teaching.
  • Prepare supplemental materials (no more than 10-15%) with current events and/or relevant past experiences for USNCC Dean and/or Associate Dean of the Academics Program approval; upload all materials onto USNCC LMS.
  • Teach assigned undergraduate-level online asynchronous courses in accordance with USNCC policies, syllabi, and instructional standards.
  • Deliver instruction using the USNCC Blackboard Learning Management System (LMS) using the government-provided course shell that includes instructional materials, core lectures, assignments, rubrics, and threaded discussion topics.
  • Facilitate engaging online discussions that encourage critical thinking and active student participation.
  • Grade assignments, examinations, discussion posts, and projects using established grading rubrics.
  • Provide detailed written feedback that promotes student learning and academic success.
  • Monitor student progress throughout the course and proactively identify students who may be at academic risk.
  • Communicate regularly with students and respond to inquiries within established response time requirements.
  • Maintain weekly virtual office hours and additional flexible office hours as needed to support student success.
  • Prepare a weekly progress report.
  • Submit all grades and required documentation within prescribed deadlines.
  • Prepare end-of-course reports summarizing student performance and recommendations for course improvements.
  • Participate in faculty meetings and collaborate with Course Leads, Academic Affairs, and Student Services when required.
  • Maintain current knowledge within the assigned discipline through professional development, scholarship, research, or participation in professional organizations.
  • Ensure all instructional materials and supplemental content comply with USNCC academic policies, copyright requirements, and Department of the Navy standards.

What qualifications do you look for?

You might be the professional we’re looking for if you have:

  • Authorization to permanently work in the United States without sponsorship.
  • Relevant military experience or similar experience in government, and/or working with military personnel.
  • Experience teaching at the collegiate level, in an online learning environment using Learning Management Systems (Blackboard or similar LMS).
  • Appropriate academic credentials and a record of scholarship/research consistent with the assigned teaching role:
    • Demonstrated expertise in military ethics, philosophy, leadership, law (post JD degree, such as, LLM in military law), U.S. history, and political science.
  • Prior experience teaching introductory courses in law of warfare, international law, military ethics, leadership, organizational behavior, law of the sea and freedom of navigation, and security studies.
  • Required Academic OR Professional Qualifications (see below).

Academic Qualifications:

Professional Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated teaching experience in an online modality for working adults; must include experience teaching one semester-equivalent course specifically in an online higher education environment at an accredited college or university demonstrating strong student and/or peer evaluation.
  • Demonstrated understanding of Andragogy and Adult Learning Theory.
  • Significant and substantive relevant experience in a military or related setting that makes you uniquely or substantively qualified to teach the specific subject area. This will typically include at least 10-15 years of direct field experience, with at least five of those years at a senior leadership level, in the specific course area being taught.

We are extraimpressed by folks with:

What kind of benefits does Terrestris Offer?

Our award programs acknowledge employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our service standards. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefit programs. Other offerings may be provided for employees not within this category.

Terrestris is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: Patent Docketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Aurora Patents is seeking an experienced patent docketing professional to take primary ownership of our U.
jobs.description:
Aurora Patents is seeking an experienced patent docketing professional to take primary ownership of our U.S. and International patent prosecution docket.

As Aurora's primary docketing professional and authority, you will independently own the integrity, administration, monitoring, and day-to-day operation of the firm's patent prosecution docket. As a core member of our firm’s three-person support team, you will be responsible for the firm's docketing system, processes, controls, integrity, and execution. This is not simply a data-entry, calendaring, or niche specialty position. We are looking for someone who understands patent prosecution well enough to independently review correspondence, identify and calculate deadlines, verify the accuracy of our docket, spot inconsistencies, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks, while helping to shape and evolve a critical part of the safeguards that protect our clients' patent rights.

What we do.

We are a patent boutique that specializes in working with early-stage med device, digital health, software, and life science companies to develop valuable patent portfolios through highly tailored, comprehensive strategies. We scale with our clients' needs and deeply understand the nuances of technology and patent strategy—and how to tie them effectively to business objectives.

Who we are.

We are a fully distributed company with a culture that promotes a high degree of autonomy, work ownership, and quality at every step. You work where, when, and how you want—with others who have a deep passion for technology.

We operate differently from a traditional law firm. Our team is collaborative, highly accessible, and intentionally low on hierarchy. That freedom comes with an expectation of ownership: when something is yours, we expect you to understand it, drive it forward, identify problems before they become problems, and communicate clearly with the people who depend on you.

What you'll do.

Your primary responsibility will be owning the integrity and day-to-day hands-on operation of Aurora's patent prosecution docket, including:

  • Docket Ownership & Deadline Management. Review and analyze incoming and outgoing correspondence relating to U.S., PCT, and foreign patent prosecution; identify, calculate, enter, update, and clear statutory and procedural deadlines; monitor upcoming deadlines; and proactively ensure responsible team members are aware of required actions. Docket and deadline management is in collaboration with BHIP Hills A.I.
  • Correspondence Intake & Triage. Manage the intake and triage of USPTO, WIPO, foreign associate, client, and practitioner correspondence, ensuring information is routed appropriately, docketed accurately, and acted upon in a timely manner.
  • Independent Docket Verification. Review prosecution status and official records using Patent Center, WIPO/PATENTSCOPE, EPO Register, foreign patent office resources, and other appropriate sources to verify bibliographic information, priority claims, application status, and outstanding deadlines.
  • Quality Control & Auditing. Conduct routine quality-control audits of docket entries, deadline calculations, bibliographic information, and matter status. Reconcile the docket against official records and source documents, investigate discrepancies, and drive issues through resolution before they create risk of abandonment or loss of rights.
  • Docket Reporting & Follow-Through. Prepare and maintain useful reports showing upcoming deadlines, outstanding actions, portfolio status, and other information needed by practitioners and management. Follow up when necessary rather than simply generating a report and moving on.
  • Matter Intake & Transfers. Establish and verify docket records for new applications, new clients, and transferred matters, including reconstructing prosecution histories where necessary and independently identifying outstanding obligations and deadlines.
  • Process Ownership & Improvement. Help us continuously improve docketing procedures, checklists, controls, and workflows. If you see a recurring source of risk or inefficiency, we want you to raise it and help us fix it.
  • Patent Portfolio Support. Work closely with our patent practitioners and prosecution paralegals to keep portfolio information accurate and current and help create meaningful portfolio insights for our clients.
  • Procure Signatures. Secure signatures on important filing and patent prosecution documents for the filing paralegal and outside law firms associated with our clients.
  • Patent Application & Prosecution Filings. As needed, prepare and file U.S. and international patent applications and prosecution documents, including formal documents such as declarations, assignments, powers of attorney, petitions, IDSs, and other supporting documents.

Who you are.

You are someone who understands that a reliable patent docket is a risk-management system, not just a calendar. And you’re looking for role ownership at a work home that operates more like a scrappy startup than an oppressive law firm. Ideally, you'll also be a good mix of the following:

  • Experienced Patent Docketing Professional. You have significant experience independently docketing U.S. and international patent prosecution matters. Ideally, you have 4+ years of patent prosecution support experience, including substantial responsibility for docket management.
  • Deadline Expert. You understand how to identify and calculate patent prosecution deadlines from source correspondence rather than relying blindly on automated docketing rules. You know the difference between a reminder and a statutory deadline and understand when extensions are, and are not, available.
  • Prosecution Fluent. You are comfortable with the lifecycle of U.S., PCT, and foreign patent applications and recognize the significance of common prosecution events, including office actions, restriction requirements, notices to file missing parts, allowances, issue fees, continuation/divisional deadlines, PCT national-phase deadlines, priority deadlines, IDS obligations, and related prosecution events.
  • Experienced with Official Patent Systems. You know your way around Patent Center and have experience researching matters using resources such as WIPO/PATENTSCOPE, EPO Register, Global Dossier, and foreign patent office databases.
  • Quality-Control Minded. You don't assume that an entry is correct because someone else entered it. You routinely reconcile information against source documents, recognize when something doesn't look right, investigate discrepancies, and close the loop.
  • Technology Comfortable. Experience with a dedicated IP docketing system is required. AppColl experience is strongly preferred, but we can train an otherwise exceptional docketing professional. Experience with Trello, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and modern project-management tools is helpful.
  • An Effective Sleuth. You can locate bibliographic and prosecution information from almost any jurisdiction and aren't stopped by incomplete records, an unfamiliar patent office website, or a matter that arrived without a perfectly organized file.
  • Hyper-Organized, Crisp Communicator. You can manage a large number of concurrent deadlines without losing sight of what matters most and can clearly communicate issues, risks, and required actions to practitioners and other team members.
  • Hungry for Autonomy. You can self-direct, prioritize, follow through, and take personal ownership of results. Prior experience working remotely in a distributed environment is helpful.
  • Proactive. You don't view your responsibility as ending when a deadline is placed on a docket. If something appears stalled, inconsistent, overdue, or at risk, you speak up and help drive it to resolution.
  • Detail-Focused. You have an exceptionally high level of attention to detail and accuracy. Small discrepancies bother you - in a good way.
  • Willing to learn. In a backup capacity, you can learn filing procedures in order to be a support when necessary to meet critical statutory deadlines if there is an overflow of filings or the filing paralegal is unavailable.
  • Highly Collaborative and People-First. You enjoy supporting practitioners, inventors, clients, and fellow paralegals; thrive as part of the solution even when things aren’t perfect (yet!); and take pride in making the entire team more effective.

Opportunity.

This is a fully remote, full-time role with a flexible workweek. The position is salaried for a guaranteed 40 hours per week. Straight-time overtime is paid for any hours above. For the right candidate, we’d also be open to considering a salaried, part-time role.

  • Full-time salary range: $85,000-$100,000
  • Benefits include 401k with match, paid time off, and profit sharing. We do not currently offer medical insurance.

Focus note: We're looking for a dedicated W-2 team member—not someone seeking overflow docketing work or a contract docketing engagement.

Location Note: Some job boards require us to specify a city, but we're fully distributed, so you can work from any reasonably well-Internet-connected location in the U.S.

Salary: $85,000 – $100,000 / year

  • Fluent in English and Spanish, with strong verbal and written communication skills in both languages.

  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency with computers, electronic health/dental records, and dental practice management software.
  • Ability to work independently and maintain productivity in a fully remote environment.
  • HIPAA knowledge or certification is preferred.

Experience with one or more of the following dental practice management systems is highly preferred:

  • Dentrix / Dentrix Ascend
  • Eaglesoft
  • Open Dental
  • Curve Dental
  • Or other comparable dental practice management systems.

Preferred Additional Experience

  • Dental insurance claims and follow-up.
  • Dental pre-authorizations and pre-determinations.
  • Treatment plan coordination.
  • Dental coding and CDT codes.
  • Understanding of dental X-rays and radiographic terminology.
  • Insurance benefit breakdowns and verification.
  • Patient billing, payment processing, and outstanding balance follow-up.
  • Experience communicating with U.S. dental insurance providers.
  • Previous remote dental practice experience.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a bilingual dental professional with strong front-office experience who can confidently communicate with patients, verify dental insurance benefits, navigate pre-authorization requirements, understand CDT codes and dental terminology, and provide administrative support with minimal supervision.

This is not a general medical receptionist position. Hands-on dental practice experience and practical knowledge of dental insurance processes are essential.
